recent_posts.title: Azure Cosmos DB Conf 2026 Highlights
recent_posts.summary: Highlights from Azure Cosmos DB Conf 2026 cover AI-driven reliability, security, and performance priorities. Key themes include AI-assisted data model review, cost reduction strategies (over 60% savings reported), vector search capabilities using the DiskANN algorithm, hybrid and full-text search, and scaling from zero to petabytes. A notable session shares a war story about building an AI system that was too costly and how it was optimized. The event also touched on vibe-coded applications going viral and the architectural importance of memory decisions for cost, recall quality, and user experience.

recent_posts.title: Build a Unity Game with GitHub Copilot + MCP | .NET Game Development
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using GitHub Copilot with the Unity MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to build a simple Unity game without leaving VS Code. The Unity MCP server lets Copilot interact directly with the Unity editor for scene management, material creation, profiler access, and more. Setup involves installing the Unity AI Assistant package, configuring the MCP relay in VS Code, and optionally adding Copilot instruction files, custom agents, and skills for better results. A live demo shows Copilot creating a ground plane, coloring objects, placing collectible coins, writing player movement scripts, and adding coin collection logic — all through natural language prompts. Custom MCP tools like domain reload triggering, game-camera screenshots, and input injection are also discussed as extensions.

recent_posts.title: Upgrade Java, Spring, and Jakarta EE with GitHub Copilot
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using GitHub Copilot's agentic upgrade feature in IntelliJ to migrate a legacy Spring Boot 1.5.9 / Java 8 application all the way to Spring Boot 3.5.3 and Java 25. The process uses OpenRewrite under the hood and proceeds through multiple milestones (Java 21 → 25, Spring Boot 3.3 → 3.4 → 3.5), running CVE checks and all 96 tests at each step. Minor Mockito 5.x compatibility issues are resolved automatically by the agent, and the full upgrade completes in roughly 20 minutes.

recent_posts.title: Make SSMS 22 Work For You: How to Customize Your Environment | Data Exposed
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of customization options in SQL Server Management Studio 22 (SSMS 22), covering both visual and workflow settings. Topics include switching color themes (including dark mode and new themes like 'bubblegum'), adjusting font sizes and presenter mode, changing null value cell highlight colors, enabling map mode for the script editor, configuring column headers when saving or dragging results to Excel/JSON, and setting group-by-schema as a default in Object Explorer. A new embedded settings experience with search and sync capabilities is also previewed.

recent_posts.title: Successfully Migrate Workloads from AWS to Azure
recent_posts.summary: A structured interview with a Microsoft partner solution architect covering three key principles for migrating workloads from AWS to Azure. The discussion highlights common failure modes: overengineering, poor stakeholder alignment, and risky big-bang cutovers. Recommended practices include starting with a readiness assessment, keeping the existing team in charge of the migration, migrating like-for-like before modernizing, and using a blue-green deployment strategy to enable safe rollback. The guidance follows a five-phase process: plan, prepare, execute, evaluate, and decommission.

recent_posts.title: Did anyone in the ’90s expect Win32 to still be a first‑class API surface in 2026?
recent_posts.summary: A reflection on the unexpected longevity of Win32 as a first-class Windows API surface in 2026, originally designed for Windows 95. The discussion covers Microsoft's failed attempts to replace it (e.g., WinRT), and draws a parallel with SysInternals tools — created in 1996 — which remain highly relevant today, with Sysmon being integrated into Windows itself and ZoomIt becoming part of PowerToys.

recent_posts.title: Assess Java Applications for Cloud Migration and Modernization
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of using GitHub Copilot's app modernization extension to assess a legacy Java monolith (built with Struts, Java 1.5, JSPs) for cloud migration. The demo shows how Copilot scans a project, runs 286 static analysis rules, and produces a dashboard report identifying cloud readiness issues, Java upgrade gaps, and tech debt — turning weeks of manual assessment into hours. The tool categorizes risks, highlights Microsoft-provided solutions, and enables custom repeatable workflows for modernization planning.

recent_posts.title: Java Application Modernization - Series Introduction
recent_posts.summary: Introduction to a new video series on modernizing Java applications using the GitHub Copilot Modernize extension. The series covers the full modernization lifecycle: assessment, framework upgrades, database migration, containerization, and CI/CD pipeline automation. The host frames modernization as a business-critical prerequisite for AI adoption, noting that 94% of executives see AI as critical but only 28% have scaled pilots to production. The workflow integrates portfolio assessment tools (Dr. Migrate, CAST, Azure Migrate), GitHub Issues, and AI agents to automate repetitive tasks like dependency updates, CVE fixes, and configuration migration — all within existing developer IDEs.

recent_posts.title: Containerization Assist Integration with AKS VSCode Extension
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of the Containerization Assist (CA) feature integrated into the Azure Kubernetes Service VS Code extension. CA is an AI-powered tool that analyzes a source code repository, detects language, framework, and dependencies, then generates production-grade Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests. The demo shows a Spring Boot app being containerized end-to-end: generating deployment files via GitHub Copilot models, setting up an Azure Container Registry, configuring OIDC-based managed identity for pipeline access, generating a GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow, and creating a pull request — all from within VS Code. Upcoming work includes monorepo support for multi-module deployments.
